title: RoPE: Rotary Position Embedding
hook: Encode position by rotating query/key vectors - relative distances then fall out of the dot product for free, no extra tokens or additive embeddings needed.
key_points: Rotates query and key vectors by an angle proportional to their absolute position before the dot product.
Relative position between two tokens emerges naturally from the inner product, without explicit relative-position tables.
Extrapolates better to longer sequences than learned absolute embeddings.
Now standard in most modern LLMs including LLaMA, Mistral, and Gemma.
content_html: Su et al. proposed Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) as a new way to inject position information into Transformer attention. Rather than adding a position vector to token embeddings, RoPE multiplies query and key vectors by a rotation matrix whose angle scales with token position. The result: relative distance between any two positions falls out of the standard dot-product attention score automatically.
extra_html:
How it works

Each query and key vector is split into pairs of dimensions, then each pair is rotated by an angle that is a fixed function of the token's position and the dimension index. When you take the dot product of a rotated query at position m and a rotated key at position n, the rotation angles partially cancel, leaving a term that depends only on the relative offset m - n. No learned position parameters are required.

Why it matters

Absolute position embeddings treat position 1 and position 1001 as unrelated; RoPE bakes relative distance into the geometry of the attention kernel itself, which improves both task performance and length generalization. Its efficiency and simplicity made it the de facto standard for open-weight LLMs. Read the full derivation on arXiv.
